_comment: Run template for b4b-windesheim: three office rooms (ROOM_<id>) and, for two of them, the same room judged on its second, desk-mounted CO2 sensor (ROOM_<id>_scd41). dcv_verification reads the ventilation valve opening (a position, not a flow) against room CO2 over the PIR-occupied intervals. The valve opens on a weekday-morning schedule AND on CO2 (see the known issues), and the rule's median CO2 lift between raised-valve and floor-valve samples mixes the two: expect 'OA modulates, but not with demand' on the BMS sensor of both rooms and 'functioning' on room 999169's SCD41 -- a verdict that depends on which sensor you trust. Room 925038 carries no OA signal (its valve column is an assumed constant; see the data issues), so the DCV rule does not evaluate it. No oa_floor_cfm: the OA signal is a position. No outdoor temperature is mapped, so the rule does not infer economizer periods for a valve that is no economizer (it notes the missing economizer signal as a caveat). co2_ventilation reads each room's CO2 against an assumed 420 ppm outdoor level: with the rooms occupied 8-14% of the time and the valve's 20% minimum still moving about 48 m3/h, CO2 near outdoor reads as over-ventilation (an energy observation, not a fault); the publisher's baseline shift moves the absolute CO2 by a constant. 15-minute resample (the publisher's interval; 3-4 weeks of data). Not run: ventilation_rate_62_1 (no measured airflow) and drift rules (too short).
